clue.text: Erring ringer with half tale extending beyond biography

indicators.note: erring means going astray, so the letters that follow wander out of their order

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer who strays, tells half a story, and stretches it past the bounds of a life story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erring' rearranges the letters of RINGER, HALF and TALE together; 'with' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: LIFE is a biography, so something larger than one goes beyond it: an idiom for exaggerated or flamboyant.

clue.text: Wodehouse's 22's autobiography, a bit at a time

definitions.meaning: 22 is BINGO, and Bingo Little is a P. G. Wodehouse character, so his life story would be a book by Little

explanation.surface: A Wodehouse character's memoirs, written slowly in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: Bingo Little is Bertie Wooster's friend in Wodehouse's stories; an autobiography of 'Little' would be written 'by Little'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning gradually, step by small step.

clue.text: Punishment about a cab I left on which I should be paid

definitions.text: on which I should be paid

indicators.note: about means around, so the rod goes round the next piece

parts.note: a rod is a traditional instrument of punishment, hence punishment itself

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I named in the clue goes away from the cab word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A fine imposed for abandoning a taxi, and a demand for payment from the car itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' of the definition is the car speaking; the same I is the letter that leaves TAXI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, road tax is the annual duty owed on a vehicle, the thing a car would say must be paid on it.

clue.text: Get tanned via the web — modern way

indicators.note: way here suggests something out of the way or odd, signalling the preceding letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip for getting a tan through some newfangled online method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' rearranges the letters of WEB and MODERN; 'Get' and 'via the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrown is to make brown, so a person made brown by the sun has become suntanned.

clue.text: Trade union going leftward as instructed

parts.note: read as 'to red': moving towards the Reds, the political left

explanation.surface: A union lurching to the left, as its members were told to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going leftward' splits as TO RED, heading for the Reds, which is the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been taught by a private teacher has been instructed.

clue.text: Encouragement to strike raised in case of a trifle

indicators.note: the toy word serves as a case, holding the turned strike word

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the strike word runs backwards

parts.note: to bat is to strike a ball

explanation.surface: A cheer of encouragement to lift and strike inside the bowl of a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' turns the strike word upwards. The trifle is not the pudding but a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of praise urging someone on, chiefly American slang for well done.

clue.text: Yarn from Innisfree?

parts.note: Yeats wrote of The Lake Isle of Innisfree; lake abbreviates to L, and adding isle gives a kind of fine cotton thread

explanation.surface: A story told by someone from Yeats's island.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarn suggests a tale, but it is a thread; 'from Innisfree' points to Yeats's poem The Lake Isle of Innisfree, L + ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves, so a yarn.

clue.text: Perplex and deceive, accepting endless cry of surprise

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the fox word holds the next piece

parts.note: to fox someone is to deceive or outwit them

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the cry is dropped

parts.note: lummy is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'lumme'

explanation.surface: Confuse and trick someone, while letting them gasp in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Lummy is an old British exclamation, like 'lor' or 'blimey'; 'endless' drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flummox is to baffle or bewilder, so a synonym for perplex.

clue.text: "No music", you tell the mess with haughty scorn

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone tells a scruffy group, with disdain, that no music will be played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the mess' rearranges NO MUSIC and YOU TELL; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumely is insolent contempt, so acting contumeliously is behaving with arrogant disdain.

clue.text: Dog did more than bark at little old coin

parts.note: Tray is a traditional dog's name, as in the song Old Dog Tray
a dog that went beyond barking bit

explanation.surface: A dog that bit someone over a small old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Dog Tray is a Stephen Foster song, so Tray is a standard crossword dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A traybit was a dialect name for the small silver threepenny piece, a coin of old British money.

clue.text: Tortoise makes exam turn to party

parts.note: an exam is a test
a U-turn, so U stands for turn
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A tortoise moves from an exam on to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Testudo is Latin for tortoise, also the genus of tortoises and the Roman shield formation named after its shell.

clue.text: Venetian painter's 21

definitions.meaning: Lorenzo ... was a Venetian Renaissance painter; the 's is 'is'
21 is HOUSE, a numbers game also called by this name

explanation.surface: A Venetian artist's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is HOUSE, the game of drawing numbered tickets; the 's reads as 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is both a painter's surname and a numbers game like house or bingo.

clue.text: Series of games not brilliant, being often showered on

parts.note: a rubber is a series of games in bridge or whist
matt, spelt mat, means having a dull finish, not shiny

explanation.surface: A dull run of games, while the players are rained on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showered on' looks like 'rained on' but means stood on by someone in the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-slip mat placed in a shower is often stood on by someone showering.

clue.text: Ring time? It's a celebration for Stephen

parts.note: boxing takes place in a ring
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A boxer's time in the ring is cause for a party for someone named Stephen.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day, 26 December, is St Stephen's Day, a British public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: St Stephen's feast falls on 26 December, the holiday known in Britain by this name.

clue.text: The proverbial shooter

definitions.meaning: the ... gun, an early machine gun

explanation.surface: The well-known gunman of the old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short pithy saying and the Maxim machine gun invented by Hiram Maxim.

clue.text: Day consumption — some red roses in the Alps

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
consumption is an old name for tuberculosis, TB

indicators.note: some means part of, so the last letter of the red-rose county is dropped

parts.note: the red rose is the emblem of Lancashire, abbreviated Lancs

explanation.surface: A day spent eating, with red roses blooming in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire, an English county, has the red rose as its emblem; 'some' trims LANCS to LANC.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest peak of the Alps, on the French-Italian border, is a mountain in that range.

clue.text: Russian general with the French resting place

parts.note: le is French for the
a bed is a place to rest

explanation.surface: A Russian general shares a French bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Lebed was a Russian general and politician of the 1990s.

clue.text: Made 1 across and dynamited?

definitions.meaning: 1 across is LARGER THAN LIFE; made bigger, enlarged as a photo is

explanation.surface: Something made larger than life and then blasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both enlarged, as a photograph is, and destroyed by explosion.

clue.text: Novelist from America entering the abused NHS when sick

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the America piece goes inside the jumble
abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: an article, read loosely here as the indefinite article a
US is the United States of America
sick means ill

explanation.surface: An American novelist goes into a mistreated National Health Service while unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'the' as the indefinite article is loose. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, so the surface is a complaint about British health care.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Hill is an English novelist, author of The Woman in Black.

clue.text: Firm insured for being cleaned too harshly?

annotationWithheld.why: Firm insured for being cleaned too harshly? (7): CO (firm) inside SURED gives the answer, but no clue words supply SURED; 'insured' would have to be both the container indicator and the fodder.
annotationWithheld.clue: Firm insured for being cleaned too harshly?

clue.text: I doubt if an austere person would go topless and embrace the piano

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the shortened word holds the piano letter
going topless means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: an ascetic lives a life of strict self-denial
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Doubt that a puritan would strip off and hug the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go topless' cuts the A from ASCETIC, leaving SCETIC; 'embrace' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter is one who says 'I doubt', so the definition is the doubter's own words.

clue.text: I produced absurdities, as 1 1 = 3/7ths of 17 down

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
the figure 1 written as a word

indicators.note: three of the seven letters of the other answer, the first three, are kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: 17 down is the seven-letter answer meaning cleaned harshly

explanation.surface: A playwright of the absurd boasts in a sum of figures and fractions.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOURED (17 down) has seven letters; '3/7ths of' keeps SCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Ionesco was a leading dramatist of the Theatre of the Absurd, so he speaks of producing absurdities.

clue.text: Sound horn at hospital entry, thus setter is to be relished?

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn

indicators.note: entry is the way in, so only the opening letter of hospital is used

parts.note: so means thus
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Honk a horn as you enter hospital: the setter is a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means tasty, something enjoyed with relish.

clue.text: Audience of aristocrats in stockings

indicators.note: the aristocratic letter goes inside the stockings word

parts.note: hose are stockings
U means upper class, aristocratic

explanation.surface: Spectators made up of nobles wearing stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper class' comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre audience is called the house, as in a full house.

clue.text: 21 for refuse collector on leave

indicators.note: on puts the bin before the leave piece

parts.note: a bin collects refuse
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A dustman going off on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is HOUSE, the numbers game. 'for' is a link word; the refuse collector is not a dustman but a bin.
explanation.definitionFit: House is an older name for the numbers game of bingo.

clue.text: Weary feeling causes primate to inhale oxygen

indicators.note: to inhale is to take in, so the monkey holds the oxygen

parts.note: a langur is an Asian monkey
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A monkey gasps for oxygen out of tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a feeling of listless tiredness.

clue.text: Where Caesar beat Pompey, thus grabbing a bit more writing

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the first word takes in the others

parts.note: taken as written
a PS (postscript) is a little extra writing

explanation.surface: Caesar's victory, described in a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Thapsus in North Africa was where Julius Caesar defeated Pompey's supporters in 46 BC.

clue.text: Add one to my church number before the operation

indicators.note: before puts the church and number pieces ahead of the last piece

parts.note: to append is to add
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
C is the Roman numeral 100
taken as written

explanation.surface: Add one person to my church congregation before surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a congregation but is C, 100.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of appendectomy, the surgical removal of the appendix.
